claim: Apple's blended gross margin percentage expanded from 43.3% in FY2022 to 50.1% by Q3 FY2026, a roughly 680-basis-point increase over about four years, driven by both Products (36.3% to 40.1%, +380bp) and Services (71.7% to 75.6%, +390bp) margin gains.
stance_target: Multi-year gross margin mix trajectory and how much is silicon-driven vs mix-driven
scope_conditions: Apple FY2022 (fiscal year ended Sept 24, 2022) vs Q3 FY2026 (quarter ended June 27, 2026)

claim: Services revenue grew 14.2% YoY in FY2022 ($78,129M vs $68,425M FY2021), comparable to or higher than the 12-16% quarterly YoY Services growth rates seen across FY2026, indicating the often-assumed 'Services growth deceleration' narrative is not clearly borne out when FY2026 is benchmarked against the FY2022 annual rate rather than against Services' pandemic-era peak growth.
stance_target: Services growth has structurally decelerated since FY2022
scope_conditions: Apple FY2022 annual vs FY2026 quarterly

claim: As of FY2022, Apple faced no DOJ antitrust suit (filed March 2024) and no EU Digital Markets Act investigation (opened March 2024); Epic Games litigation was still at the original district court stage, with Apple having won 9 of 10 counts in September 2021 and a cross-appeal stay pending -- a materially more benign legal-risk baseline than the FY2026 quarters' active DOJ suit, adjudicated DMA fine (EUR500M), open DMA Article 6(4) investigation exposing up to 10% of worldwide net sales, and an Epic injunction escalated to a Supreme Court certiorari grant.
stance_target: Regulatory/legal exposure to Apple's App Store commissions and platform practices has materially escalated since FY2022, independent of the underlying business
scope_conditions: Apple FY2022 10-K Item 3 Legal Proceedings vs FY2026 quarterly 10-Qs
quoted_support: On September 10, 2021, the Northern California District Court ruled in favor of the Company with respect to nine out of the ten counts included in Epic's claim, and in favor of the Company with respect to the Company's claims for breach of contract.
numbers: DMA investigations opened March 25, 2024 and June 24, 2024
DMA Article 6(4) exposure up to 10% of annual worldwide net sales

claim: Greater China grew only 8.5% YoY in FY2022 ($74,200M vs $68,366M FY2021), materially slower than the 22-38% YoY growth rates seen in each FY2026 quarter, indicating Greater China's current growth reacceleration is a recent (FY2026) phenomenon rather than a multi-year trend.
stance_target: Greater China growth trajectory over the multi-year baseline

claim: Apple's Services revenue definition explicitly includes 'advertising, AppleCare, cloud, digital content, payment and other services' as a single undifferentiated line -- Google's search-placement payment (TAC) is folded into the undisclosed advertising/other category and never broken out as a discrete dollar figure in any Apple 10-K or 10-Q reviewed.
stance_target: Audited absence: Google TAC and App Store commissions are not separately disclosed by Apple
scope_conditions: Apple FY2022 10-K, footnote 3 to net sales by category table; searched for 'Google', 'search', 'TAC', 'commission' throughout the filing -- no dollar figures found
quoted_support: Services net sales include sales from the Company's advertising, AppleCare, cloud, digital content, payment and other services.
numbers: No Google TAC dollar disclosure found
No App Store commission dollar disclosure found

claim: Apple's FY2022 capex was $10,708M and buybacks $89,402M for the full fiscal year, against R&D of $26,251M -- providing a pre-AI-era baseline against which the FY2026 pattern of rising R&D (annualizing near $45B) alongside flat-to-lower capex can be measured.
stance_target: Whether Apple's AI investment represents a step-change versus historical capital allocation patterns
